steps.prompt: Before your first full mock: what score would you be happy with, and which strand do you expect to be your strongest?
steps.placeholder: I'd be happy with… My strongest strand is…

cards.title: Taking a mock like the real thing
cards.body: Find a quiet place and $75$ minutes with no breaks. Have scrap paper and a pencil, but no calculator: the AMC 10 doesn't allow one. Use your pacing plan: a first pass with the $2$-minute rule, then the flagged problems. The clock runs on the server, so the mock hands itself in when time runs out, even if you close the page.

cards.title: Mistake analysis
cards.body: After the mock, open your result and sort every miss and blank into one of four boxes: (1) I didn't know the idea, (2) a careless slip, (3) I misread the question, (4) I ran out of time. Add the problems you didn't know to your error log, and look at the review by strand and by difficulty: is one strand weak, or do the points leak away in the last ten problems?

cards.title: Worked example: where the points went
cards.problem: Lena got $14$ right, $5$ wrong and left $6$ blank. Three of her wrong answers were careless slips. What would she have scored with those $3$ right?

steps.text: Three more right answers add $18$ points: careless slips cost the most.

prompts: Which of the four boxes held most of your misses?
